result.summary: Manual review, not a canonical CR and not BUILD approval. The input had no source text, diffs or test output. It had only file hashes, an audit inventory and UX/sequence/component definitions. So I could not check either assigned obligation against code, and I raised no defects. Both obligations are could-not-verify. The supplied metadata is consistent with both, but metadata is not evidence of the code.

obligations.evidence: Inventory lists src/shared/ipc-client.ts (hash a06f7a2c…), vscode-plugin/src/connections/session-owner.ts and gateway.ts. The component definition says 'Persistent TypeScript lanes preserve one-shot API' and 'APP gateway remains unclaimed/stateless'. No source or diff was supplied, so I could not check that the exported one-shot signatures are unchanged. I also could not check that the persistent lane reuses the same socket and backend path rather than adding a new backend or storage path. The Kotlin transport boundary file is not in the inventory at all. No existing-API compatibility test output was supplied. The design text agrees with the invariant, but it is not proof.

The inventory records releaseEnabled=false, releaseAuditStatus 'pending; independent of runtime availability', and S001, providerService, positiveSavedWorkerAffinity and SQLServer all 'pending'. JetBrainsLiveUI is 'deferred-user' and VSCodeLiveUI is 'completed-user-reported'. This is consistent with the release gate staying disabled. The user explicitly authorized runtime enablement by default (runtimeEnabled=true), and I did not reopen that decision. I could not read src/daemon/db/management-enablement.ts (hash 6869dcd2…), index.ts or the capabilities code. So I could not confirm that releaseEnabled is false in code, that runtime enablement is separate from the release gate, or that no test fixture is treated as acceptance. 'producerPolicyModified: true' also needs source to review.

inspectedFiles: Implementation definitions (UX, sequence, component dependency) — metadata only
Consumer audit inventory — hashes and statuses only
limitations: No file contents or diffs were supplied. None of the changed files in the inventory were assessed, including src/shared/ipc-client.ts, src/shared/connection-manager/*, src/daemon/db/management-*.ts, src/daemon/connection-management-rpc.ts, src/daemon/index.ts, vscode-plugin/src/connections/*, vscode-plugin/src/extension.ts, the media assets and all jetbrains-plugin connections/settings/actions files.
The Kotlin persistent transport lane and DaemonGatewayService are not listed in the inventory, so I could not check them for the one-shot compatibility invariant.
No test output was supplied, so I treated no test as evidence. The known sweep failures (S003: 8 failed, S004: 21 failed) are recorded but not tied to these obligations.
Live UI, SQL Server, provider-service and worker-affinity coverage are pending or deferred. I did not count any of them as passed.
Hashes cannot be tied to the review HEAD 90404ac8 because the inventory's sourceCommit is f5f0eafd0.
evidenceRequests: Source of src/shared/ipc-client.ts at HEAD, with its diff against the pre-change version, to compare the exported one-shot function signatures and behavior with the new persistent-lane additions.
Tests that exercise the one-shot IPC API (existing callers and the legacy JetBrains DaemonGatewayService one-shot delegation), and the Kotlin transport file containing the persistent lane.

src/daemon/db/management-enablement.ts and the capability and handshake code that computes releaseEnabled and runtime capabilities, to confirm the release gate is false and separate from runtime enablement.
Any test or config that sets releaseEnabled=true, to confirm it is fixture-only and unreachable in production.
